Gary McGURREN, Glynn Tiernan and Matthew Kinane have been mainly responsible for this effort, finishing each race with barely a vest between them all season.
It was also at this meeting that Matthew Kinane confirmed his progress this year by breaking the longstanding Club Youths Mile Record with 4.26.0 in 7th place in the Peter Coe mile.

The most significant team result was stealing a highly contested Surrey Championship title with a fine individual 4th from Garry McGurren, backed by Matthew Kinane (flying in from Switzerland hours before), Simon Beaumont and Glynn Tiernan.
Duncan Ward hands to Matthew Kinane in the winning 1984 Boys Surrey Road Relay winning team.

This meeting clashed with the London District meeting at Crystal Palace and apart from Matthew Kinane who was returning to competition after an absence for studies, robbed us of the entire Youths track team from 100m to 1500m.
Outstanding was Matthew Kinane's leg as he chased for second, producing a time only 5 seconds slower than that of Mark Sinclair in the Senior event.
